text.title: Freelancer Scope-Change Script Library Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether an agreed baseline exists, then on the shape of the request — one sizeable ask, a run of small ones, or a genuine emergency — to the rule the script must satisfy.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there an agreed commercial baseline — SOW, fixed scope, quoted price — that this request falls outside of?

branch.when: internal-team work with no commercial boundary, or the dispute is termination or unpaid invoices rather than scope

conclusion.verdict: skip; these scripts price a change against a baseline — with none, or with the contract itself in dispute, route to contract review and emit a structured skip

branch.when: a baseline exists and the request sits outside it
branch.question: What shape is the request?

branch.when: a single sizeable ask that moves cost or date on its own
branch.question: Is the deadline immovable for the client — a launch, an event, a contract date?

branch.when: yes; the date cannot move whatever the price

conclusion.verdict: offer at least two options, one of which holds date and budget by deferring a named in-scope item; the client picks what loses, so the boundary holds without a refusal

branch.when: no; both money and date are negotiable

conclusion.verdict: price the change on both axes in one line — hours and money, and the date it moves from and to; one axis alone invites payment on the axis the client considers cheap

branch.when: a run of small asks, none of them big enough to argue about individually
branch.question: Is there a log of the prior unbilled asks with hours against them?

branch.when: yes; the count and the cumulative hours can be quoted verbatim

conclusion.verdict: state the aggregate — how many prior asks, how many hours — not just this request; the pattern is the only thing that makes declining proportionate

branch.when: no log; only a felt sense that it keeps happening

conclusion.verdict: start the log, and make the next step a written change order with a decision deadline before any work begins; 'sort the paperwork later' is forbidden for this type

branch.when: a genuine crisis on the client side and an out-of-scope ask for help right now
branch.question: Does the draft reply state an end — a date or hour count — and name what gets dropped to make room?

branch.when: no; the draft says something like 'I'll take care of it'

conclusion.verdict: bound the concession in the same message with an end and a named displaced item; nobody sends a notice when the emergency is over

branch.when: the draft opens with an apology, or 'no problem / happy to fit it in' before the impact line

conclusion.verdict: label the pressure and stop; strip apology and commitment verbs, since a concession before the price sets that price at zero

branch.when: the message mixes a new ask with an existing commitment and the type is not yet clear

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; classify situation_type against the baseline first, then draft empathy, impact, options and next step and check them against the rule set
